metadata.title: Painter, Maini & Othmer (1999) Keller-Segel Chemotactic Pattern Formation, Equal-Diffusivity Instability & Domain-Growth Stripe-Splitting Reference Dataset

sources.citation: Painter KJ, Maini PK, Othmer HG (1999). Stripe and spotilihood in chemotactic pattern formation. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences USA 96(10):5549-5554.
Keller EF, Segel LA (1970). Initiation of slime mold aggregation viewed as an instability. Journal of Theoretical Biology 26(3):399-415.
Myerscough MR, Murray JD (1992). Analysis of propagating pattern in a chemotaxis system. Bulletin of Mathematical Biology 54(1):77-94.
Painter KJ, Hillen T (2011). Spatio-temporal chaos in a chemotaxis model. Physica D: Nonlinear Phenomena 240(4-5):363-375.

myxococcus_xanthus_chemotactic_stripes_a.species: Myxococcus xanthus (social bacterium exhibiting periodic chemotactic/rippling stripe ridges and fruiting-body spot aggregates, 500 um scale bar)
myxococcus_xanthus_chemotactic_stripes_a.author: Jens Boenigk / Wikimedia Commons

keller_segel_painter_1999_system.section: Painter, Maini & Othmer (1999) PNAS 96(10):5549-5554 Eqs. (1)-(6) & Figs. 1-4

governing_pde.n_eq: dn/dt = D_n * Lap(n) - div(n * chi(c) * grad(c)) + r * n * (1 - n / n_0)
governing_pde.c_eq: dc/dt = D_c * Lap(c) + alpha * n / (1 + beta * n) - gamma * c
governing_pde.chemotactic_sensitivity: chi(c) = chi_0 / (1 + kappa * c)^2  (with kappa = 0 for constant sensitivity chi(c) = chi_0)
governing_pde.boundary_condition: Zero-flux (Neumann) n_hat . grad(n) = n_hat . grad(c) = 0 on domain boundary

equal_diffusivity_theorem.statement: Unlike two-species reaction-diffusion systems where D_u = D_v strictly precludes Turing instability, the Keller-Segel-Painter chemotactic-RD system undergoes spatial pattern bifurcation at equal diffusivity D_n = D_c = D whenever n_0 * chi(c*) * s* > (sqrt(r * D_c) + sqrt(gamma * D_n))^2.

domain_growth_stripe_splitting_regimes.section: Painter, Maini & Othmer (1999) PNAS 96(10):5549-5554 Figs. 1-3 (1D & 2D Exponential/Linear Domain Growth & Mode Doubling)
domain_growth_stripe_splitting_regimes.growth_law: L(t) = L_0 * exp(rho_g * t) or discrete domain scale stages L / lambda_c in {1, 2, 4, 8}

regimes.label: Subcritical Chemotaxis Control (chi = 3.0 < chi_c = 4.5, D_n = D_c = 1.0)
regimes.description: Below critical chemotactic sensitivity chi_c = 4.5, det M(k^2) > 0 for all wavenumbers k^2 >= 0; perturbations decay to homogeneous equilibrium (n*, c*) = (1, 1).

regimes.label: Initial Domain Stage L_1 = 1 * lambda_c (s = 1)
regimes.description: At initial domain length L_1 = lambda_c = 4.443, a single interior chemotactic cell-density stripe (N = 1 peak) is stabilized.

regimes.label: First Stripe-Splitting Stage L_2 = 2 * lambda_c (s = 2)
regimes.description: As domain length doubles to 2 * lambda_c = 8.886, the trough depletes chemoattractant below threshold and the primary stripe splits / inserts into N = 2 equidistant stripes.

regimes.label: Second Stripe-Splitting Cascade L_3 = 4 * lambda_c (s = 4)
regimes.description: Second domain doubling to 4 * lambda_c = 17.772 triggers synchronous bifurcating stripe splitting from N = 2 to N = 4 peaks with invariant spacing lambda_c = 4.443.

regimes.label: Third Stripe-Splitting Cascade L_4 = 8 * lambda_c (s = 8)
regimes.description: Third domain doubling to 8 * lambda_c = 35.543 yields N = 8 periodic chemotactic cell-density stripes via continuous peak splitting.

stripe_vs_spot_selection_2d.section: Painter, Maini & Othmer (1999) PNAS 96(10):5549-5554 Section 'Stripes Versus Spots in Two Dimensions' & Fig. 4

stripe_regime.description: Symmetric cubic saturation (large beta or balanced logistic-chemotactic feedback around n = n_0) suppresses quadratic resonant triad interactions, stabilizing 2D labyrinthine chemotactic stripes.

spot_regime.description: Strong quadratic chemotactic self-focusing div(n chi grad c) with weak saturation drives hexagonal spot/fruiting-body droplets.
